test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: According to the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, how many Muslim women should be included in the State Waqf Boards?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Two**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024**, which was introduced in the **Lok Sabha** in **August 2024** and discussed extensively through **2024** and **2025**, proposes significant reforms to the **Waqf Act, 1995**.
 
• One of the primary structural changes proposed is the mandatory inclusion of **two Muslim women** in the **State Waqf Boards**. This is intended to ensure gender diversity and provide women with a voice in the management of religious and charitable endowments.
 
• The Bill mandates that the **State Waqf Board** composition must include these **two Muslim women** alongside other members appointed by the **State Government**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the inclusion of two women is correct.***
 
• In addition to women, the Bill also introduces a requirement for **two non-Muslim members** to be included in the **State Waqf Boards**, aiming for a more inclusive administrative structure.
 
• These amendments seek to replace the existing provisions where the boards were predominantly composed of members from the Muslim community without specific mandates for **women** or **non-Muslim** representation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Central Waqf Council:** The proposed legislation also modifies the composition of the **Central Waqf Council**. It mandates that the Council must include **two Muslim women** among its members to provide better oversight at the **National Level**.
 
• **Waqf Act, 1995:** This is the parent **Act** that currently governs the administration of **Auqaf** (assets donated for **Muslim** religious or charitable purposes) in **India**. The **2024-2025** amendments are the most comprehensive changes since the **2013** amendment.
 
• **Definition of Waqf:** The Bill proposes that only a person who has been practicing **Islam** for at least **five years** and owns the property can create a **Waqf**. This is a shift from the broader earlier definitions.
 
• **Waqf-alal-aulad:** The Bill addresses **Waqf-alal-aulad** (Waqf for the benefit of the donor's family), ensuring that such dedications do not lead to the deprivation of inheritance rights for **women** heirs of the donor.
 
• **Authority of the Collector:** A major feature of the **Waqf (Amendment) Bill** is granting the **District Collector** the power to determine whether a property is **Waqf property** or **Government land**, shifting this power away from the **Waqf Tribunal** in specific disputes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Removal of Waqf by User:** The Bill proposes to abolish the concept of **"Waqf by User,"** which allowed land to be declared **Waqf** simply because it had been used for religious purposes for a long **duration** without formal documentation.
 
• **Registration Process:** It makes the **registration** of all **Waqf properties** mandatory on a centralized **online portal**. This aims to increase **transparency** and reduce litigation regarding land ownership.
 
• **Separate Boards:** The Bill provides for the establishment of separate **Waqf Boards** for the **Bohra** and **Aghakhani** communities if deemed necessary, acknowledging the diversity within the **Muslim** community.
 
• **Audit and Accountability:** It introduces stricter **audit** requirements for the accounts of **Waqf Boards**, allowing the **Central Government** or **State Government** to order audits by the **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)** or designated officers.
 
• **Legal Challenges:** The Bill was referred to a **Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC)** in **2024** for detailed scrutiny due to concerns raised by various stakeholders regarding federalism and religious autonomy.
